25pub(crate) struct Type0Font {
26    font_type: FontType,
27    horizontal: bool,
28    cache_key: u128,
29    dw: f32,
30    dw2: (f32, f32),
31    widths: HashMap<u32, f32>,
32    encoding: CMap,
33    to_unicode: Option<CMap>,
34    widths2: HashMap<u32, [f32; 3]>,
35    cid_to_gid_map: CidToGIdMap,
36    /// PostScript name from the PDF.
37    postscript_name: Option<String>,
38    /// Font flags from the font descriptor.
39    font_flags: Option<FontFlags>,
40    /// Whether this font is using a fallback (non-embedded) font.
41    fallback: bool,
42    /// Whether the `to_unicode` map is a UCS2 `CMap` (CID-indexed) rather than
43    /// a `ToUnicode` `CMap` (code-indexed).
44    to_unicode_is_cid_indexed: bool,
45    /// PdfCraft patch (84): the character collection's UCS2 CMap (by CID), for the codes the
46    /// font's own `/ToUnicode` gives nothing for, whether or not its program is embedded.
47    ucs2: Option<Ucs2>,
48    /// PdfCraft patch: whether the CIDs belong to an Adobe character collection (Japan1, GB1,
49    /// CNS1, Korea1), whose glyph numbering no substitute other than a CID-keyed CFF font shares.
50    adobe_collection: bool,
51    /// PdfCraft patch: `/ToUnicode /Identity-H` (a name, not a CMap stream), which CAD exporters
52    /// such as WSCAD write for fonts whose two-byte codes are UTF-16 code units. Acrobat shows
53    /// such text as the code's Unicode value; the identity CMap the name resolves to maps codes
54    /// to CIDs only and gave no text at all.
55    identity_to_unicode: bool,
56    /// PdfCraft patch: an Arial or a Times New Roman the PDF doesn't embed, as a TrueType CID
57    /// font (`CIDFontType2`) whose CIDs aren't of an Adobe character collection. Its CIDToGIDMap
58    /// gives glyph indexes in the author's font, which numbers its first 258 glyphs in the
59    /// standard Macintosh order of the TrueType `post` table (#5889, #6449).
60    mac_glyph_order: bool,
61}

64    /// Reads a Type 0 font from its dictionary: the descendant CID font, the encoding CMap and
65    /// the code-to-Unicode map (`/ToUnicode`, the `/Identity-H` name, or the UCS2 CMap).
66    pub(crate) fn new(dict: &Dict<'_>, font_resolver: &FontResolverFn, cmap_resolver: &CMapResolverFn) -> Option<Self> {
67        let cmap = read_encoding(&dict.get::<Object<'_>>(ENCODING)?, cmap_resolver)?;
68
69        let horizontal = cmap.metadata().writing_mode != Some(WritingMode::Vertical);
70
71        let descendant_font = dict.get::<Array<'_>>(DESCENDANT_FONTS)?.iter::<Dict<'_>>().next()?;
72        let font_descriptor = descendant_font.get::<Dict<'_>>(FONT_DESC).unwrap_or_default();
73
74        let character_collection = cmap
75            .metadata()
76            .character_collection
77            .clone()
78            .filter(|cc| cc.family != CidFamily::AdobeIdentity)
79            .or_else(|| read_cid_system_info(&descendant_font));
80
81        let (font_type, fallback, _is_standard_fallback) = match FontType::new(&font_descriptor) {
82            Some(ft) => (ft, false, false),
83            None => {
84                let (query, is_standard) = if let Some((standard, _)) = select_standard_font(dict, &font_descriptor) {
85                    (FontQuery::Standard(standard), true)
86                } else {
87                    // PdfCraft patch: the style comes from the descendant's descriptor.
88                    let mut query = FallbackFontQuery::with_descriptor(dict, Some(font_descriptor.clone()));
89                    query.character_collection = character_collection.clone();
90
91                    warn!(
92                        "unable to load CID font {} ({:?}), attempting fallback",
93                        query.post_script_name.as_deref().unwrap_or("(no name)"),
94                        dict.obj_id()
95                    );
96
97                    (FontQuery::Fallback(query), false)
98                };
99
100                let (data, index) = font_resolver(&query)?;
101                let blob =
102                    OpenTypeFontBlob::new(data.clone(), index).map(FontType::OpenType).or_else(|| CffFontBlob::new(data).map(FontType::Cff))?;
103                (blob, true, is_standard)
104            }
105        };
106
107        let default_width = descendant_font.get::<f32>(DW).unwrap_or(1000.0);
108        let dw2 = descendant_font.get::<[f32; 2]>(DW2).map(|v| (v[0], v[1])).unwrap_or((880.0, -1000.0));
109
110        let widths = descendant_font.get::<Array<'_>>(W).and_then(|a| read_widths(&a)).unwrap_or_default();
111        let widths2 = descendant_font.get::<Array<'_>>(W2).and_then(|a| read_widths2(&a)).unwrap_or_default();
112        let cid_to_gid_map = CidToGIdMap::new(&descendant_font).unwrap_or_default();
113        let cache_key = dict.cache_key();
114
115        let mut to_unicode = read_to_unicode(dict, cmap_resolver);
116        let identity_to_unicode = dict.get::<Name<'_>>(TO_UNICODE).is_some_and(|n| matches!(n.as_ref(), b"Identity-H" | b"Identity-V"));
117        let mut to_unicode_is_cid_indexed = false;
118
119        // PdfCraft patch (84): the character collection's UCS2 CMap (ISO 32000-2 §9.10.2), CID
120        // to Unicode, for a font of an Adobe collection whether or not its program is embedded.
121        let mut ucs2 = character_collection.as_ref().and_then(|cc| cc.family.ucs2_cmap()).and_then(|name| (cmap_resolver)(name)).map(|data| Ucs2 {
122            data,
123            resolver: cmap_resolver.clone(),
124            map: OnceLock::new(),
125        });
126        // If there is no ToUnicode map, try to get the UCS2 CMap.
127        if fallback
128            && to_unicode.is_none()
129            && let Some(ucs2_cmap) = ucs2.take().and_then(|u| u.parse())
130        {
131            to_unicode = Some(ucs2_cmap);
132            to_unicode_is_cid_indexed = true;
133        }
134
135        let adobe_collection = character_collection.as_ref().is_some_and(|cc| cc.family.ucs2_cmap().is_some());
136
137        let postscript_name = dict.get::<Name<'_>>(BASE_FONT).map(|n| strip_subset_prefix(n.as_str()).to_string());
138
139        // PdfCraft patch: the descendant names the font program itself; a Type 0 font's own
140        // `/BaseFont` may carry the CMap's name after it.
141        let mac_glyph_order = fallback
142            && !adobe_collection
143            && descendant_font.get::<Name<'_>>(SUBTYPE).is_some_and(|s| s.deref() == CID_FONT_TYPE2)
144            && descendant_font.get::<Name<'_>>(BASE_FONT).is_some_and(|n| numbers_glyphs_in_mac_order(strip_subset_prefix(n.as_str())));
145
146        // Extract font flags from descriptor
147        let font_flags = font_descriptor.get::<u32>(FLAGS).and_then(FontFlags::from_bits);
148
149        Some(Self {
150            cache_key,
151            horizontal,
152            encoding: cmap,
153            to_unicode,
154            font_type,
155            dw: default_width,
156            dw2,
157            widths,
158            widths2,
159            cid_to_gid_map,
160            postscript_name,
161            font_flags,
162            fallback,
163            to_unicode_is_cid_indexed,
164            ucs2,
165            adobe_collection,
166            identity_to_unicode,
167            mac_glyph_order,
168        })
169    }

171    pub(crate) fn map_code(&self, code: u32) -> GlyphId {
172        let Some(cid) = self.code_to_cid(code) else {
173            return GlyphId::NOTDEF;
174        };
175
176        // UCS2 maps are indexed by CIDs, while embededd `ToUnicode` maps are
177        // indexed by character code.
178        let to_unicode_key = if self.to_unicode_is_cid_indexed { cid } else { code };
179
180        if self.fallback
181            && let Some(glyph) = self.map_via_unicode(to_unicode_key)
182        {
183            // Yay, Unicode worked!
184            return glyph;
185        }
186
187        // PdfCraft patch: the CID of an Arial or a Times New Roman the PDF doesn't embed names
188        // one of that font's glyphs, which the substitute draws by that name. Taken as the
189        // substitute's own glyph index it drew an unrelated glyph: "Low Power" as
190        // "@ck 'Dck Yf" (#5889), "Salarié(e) du régime" as "Salari²*g+f w't²i lo" (#6449).
191        if self.mac_glyph_order
192            && let Some(glyph) = self.map_via_mac_glyph_name(cid)
193        {
194            return glyph;
195        }
196
197        // PdfCraft patch: a substitute that isn't CID-keyed numbers its glyphs its own way, so
198        // the CID of an Adobe character collection taken as its glyph index draws an unrelated
199        // glyph. Draw .notdef, as for a CID the font has no glyph for.
200        if self.fallback && self.adobe_collection && !matches!(&self.font_type, FontType::Cff(c) if c.is_cid()) {
201            return GlyphId::NOTDEF;
202        }
203
204        // At this point, not much we can do anymore. Just hope that the
205        // selected font has the right glyph order, and map via that.
206
207        match &self.font_type {
208            FontType::OpenType(_) => self.cid_to_gid_map.map(cid as u16),
209            FontType::Cff(c) => {
210                if c.is_cid() {
211                    // Very confusing stuff going on here, see https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/pull/15563.
212                    // The PDF spec makes it sounds like cid-to-gid map should only be used for TrueType fonts,
213                    // but Acrobat also seems to support it for CFF fonts with some weird behavior.
214                    if matches!(self.cid_to_gid_map, CidToGIdMap::Identity) {
215                        c.glyph_index_by_cid(cid as u16).unwrap_or(GlyphId::NOTDEF)
216                    } else {
217                        GlyphId::new(self.cid_to_gid_map.inverse_map(GlyphId::new(cid)) as u32)
218                    }
219                } else {
220                    self.cid_to_gid_map.map(cid as u16)
221                }
222            }
223            // Maybe we need similar processing to CFF fonts? But since
224            // Type1 fonts are invalid anyway, let's just ignore for now.
225            FontType::Type1(_) => GlyphId::new(cid),
226        }
227    }

229    /// Map a character code (or CID) to a glyph ID
230    /// by first getting its Unicode and then looking up the codepoint in the
231    /// font's cmap.
232    fn map_via_unicode(&self, key: u32) -> Option<GlyphId> {
233        let to_unicode = self.to_unicode.as_ref()?;
234
235        let (character, selector) = to_unicode
236            .lookup_bf_string(key)
237            .or_else(|| {
238                for len in 0..4 {
239                    if let Some(code) = to_unicode.lookup_cid_code(key, len)
240                        && let Some(code) = char::from_u32(code.to_u32())
241                    {
242                        return Some(BfString::Char(code));
243                    }
244                }
245
246                None
247            })
248            .and_then(|bf| match bf {
249                BfString::Char(c) => Some((c, None)),
250                // PdfCraft patch: a character and a variation selector is that character in a
251                // given form, as Adobe-Japan1 maps the JIS X 0208 forms of the kanji that
252                // JIS X 0213:2004 redrew (噂 is U+5642 U+E0100). Other strings (ligatures) still
253                // have no glyph.
254                BfString::String(s) => {
255                    let mut chars = s.chars();
256                    let character = chars.next()?;
257                    let selector = chars.next().filter(|c| is_variation_selector(*c))?;
258                    chars.next().is_none().then_some((character, Some(selector)))
259                }
260            })?;
261
262        match &self.font_type {
263            FontType::OpenType(t) => {
264                let charmap = t.font_ref().charmap();
265                // PdfCraft patch: the face's glyph for that form when its `cmap` has one, else its
266                // glyph for the character, as when a form isn't supported (Unicode FAQ on
267                // variation sequences).
268                if let Some(selector) = selector
269                    && let Some(MapVariant::Variant(glyph)) = charmap.map_variant(character, selector)
270                {
271                    return Some(glyph);
272                }
273                // PdfCraft patch: a substitute may lack a spacing character (#3601; e.g.
274                // Adobe-Japan1's U+2002). Draw its ordinary space instead of .notdef;
275                // the PDF's widths and Unicode mapping still determine advance and text.
276                charmap.map(character).or_else(|| match character {
277                    '\u{00a0}' | '\u{2000}'..='\u{200a}' | '\u{202f}' | '\u{205f}' | '\u{3000}' => charmap.map(' '),
278                    _ => None,
279                })
280            }
281            FontType::Cff(c) => {
282                // Map codepoint to glyph name via AFL, and then look it up.
283                let by_name = |character: char| glyph_names::get_reverse(character).and_then(|name| c.glyph_index_by_name(name));
284                // PdfCraft patch: a soft hyphen the substitute has no glyph for is its hyphen
285                // (#5888). Windows exporters map the hyphen glyph of a font they don't embed to
286                // U+00AD, which ISO 32000-2 Annex D.2 calls typographically the same as the
287                // hyphen; without this the CID, taken as a glyph index, drew an unrelated glyph.
288                by_name(character).or_else(|| (character == '\u{00ad}').then(|| by_name('-')).flatten())
289            }
290            FontType::Type1(_) => {
291                // We could in theory map to a glyph via AFL and then look up
292                // the glyph index in the encoding, but since skrifa doesn't have
293                // an API for that and this is only really necessary for fallback
294                // fonts (which currently only supports OpenType and CFF as fallback),
295                // so we don't support this for now.
296                None
297            }
298        }
299    }

301    /// PdfCraft patch: the substitute's glyph for the author's glyph that `cid` gives, found by
302    /// that glyph's name in the standard Macintosh order. `None` past the 258 glyphs the order
303    /// names, and for a substitute that isn't a name-keyed CFF font (the standard substitutes
304    /// are); .notdef for a name the substitute has no glyph for.
305    fn map_via_mac_glyph_name(&self, cid: u32) -> Option<GlyphId> {
306        let FontType::Cff(c) = &self.font_type else {
307            return None;
308        };
309        if c.is_cid() {
310            return None;
311        }
312        let gid = self.cid_to_gid_map.map(u16::try_from(cid).ok()?);
313        let name = *DEFAULT_GLYPH_NAMES.get(usize::try_from(gid.to_u32()).ok()?)?;
314        // `.null` and `nonmarkingreturn` draw nothing, and `nonbreakingspace` is a space.
315        let name = match name {
316            ".null" | "nonmarkingreturn" | "nonbreakingspace" => "space",
317            name => name,
318        };
319        Some(c.glyph_index_by_name(name).unwrap_or(GlyphId::NOTDEF))
320    }

322    fn code_to_cid(&self, code: u32) -> Option<u32> {
323        for byte_len in 1..=4_u8 {
324            if let Some(cid) = self.encoding.lookup_cid_code(code, byte_len) {
325                return Some(cid);
326            }
327        }
328
329        None
330    }

332    pub(crate) fn outline_glyph(&self, glyph: GlyphId, code: u32) -> BezPath {
333        let path = match &self.font_type {
334            FontType::OpenType(t) => t.outline_glyph(glyph),
335            FontType::Cff(c) => c.outline_glyph(glyph),
336            FontType::Type1(t) => t.outline_glyph(glyph),
337        };
338
339        if self.fallback
340            && let FontType::OpenType(t) = &self.font_type
341            && let Some(cid) = self.code_to_cid(code)
342            && let Some(actual_width) = t.glyph_metrics().advance_width(glyph)
343            // Only use an expected width if there is an explicit /W array,
344            // not the default width, as it leads to weird results from my testing.
345            && let Some(expected_width) = self.widths.get(&cid).copied()
346        {
347            return stretch_glyph(path, expected_width, actual_width);
348        }
349
350        path
351    }

366    /// Get the font weight (100-900, 400=normal, 700=bold).
367    ///
368    /// Returns `None` if weight cannot be determined (CFF fonts or invalid weight).
369    pub(crate) fn weight(&self) -> Option<u32> {
370        match &self.font_type {
371            FontType::OpenType(t) => {
372                let weight = t.font_ref().attributes().weight.value().round() as u32;
373                if weight > 0 { Some(weight) } else { None }
374            }
375            FontType::Cff(_) | FontType::Type1(_) => None,
376        }
377    }

379    /// Check if font is italic based on font flags or font attributes.
380    pub(crate) fn is_italic(&self) -> bool {
381        if let Some(flags) = &self.font_flags
382            && flags.contains(FontFlags::ITALIC)
383        {
384            return true;
385        }
386        match &self.font_type {
387            FontType::OpenType(t) => t.font_ref().attributes().style != Style::Normal,
388            FontType::Cff(_) | FontType::Type1(_) => false,
389        }
390    }
391
392    /// Check if font is serif based on font flags.
393    pub(crate) fn is_serif(&self) -> bool {
394        self.font_flags.as_ref().is_some_and(|f| f.contains(FontFlags::SERIF))
395    }

397    /// Check if font is monospace based on font flags or font metrics.
398    pub(crate) fn is_monospace(&self) -> bool {
399        if let Some(flags) = &self.font_flags
400            && flags.contains(FontFlags::FIXED_PITCH)
401        {
402            return true;
403        }
404        match &self.font_type {
405            FontType::OpenType(t) => {
406                t.font_ref().metrics(skrifa_047::instance::Size::unscaled(), skrifa_047::instance::LocationRef::default()).is_monospace
407            }
408            FontType::Cff(_) | FontType::Type1(_) => false,
409        }
410    }

412    pub(crate) fn code_advance(&self, code: u32) -> Vec2 {
413        let cid = self.code_to_cid(code).unwrap_or(0);
414        if self.horizontal {
415            Vec2::new(self.horizontal_width(cid) as f64, 0.0)
416        } else if let Some([w, _, _]) = self.widths2.get(&cid) {
417            Vec2::new(0.0, *w as f64)
418        } else {
419            Vec2::new(0.0, self.dw2.1 as f64)
420        }
421    }

423    /// PdfCraft patch: the code's width w0 (its horizontal displacement, from `/W` or `/DW`)
424    /// in either writing mode. In vertical writing it is the glyph's extent across the column
425    /// (ISO 32000-2 §9.7.4.3).
426    pub(crate) fn code_horizontal_width(&self, code: u32) -> f32 {
427        self.horizontal_width(self.code_to_cid(code).unwrap_or(0))
428    }

430    fn horizontal_width(&self, cid: u32) -> f32 {
431        self.widths.get(&cid).copied().unwrap_or(self.dw)
432    }

434    pub(crate) fn is_horizontal(&self) -> bool {

438    pub(crate) fn read_code(&self, bytes: &[u8], offset: usize) -> (u32, usize) {
439        let mut code = 0_u32;
440        let remaining = bytes.len() - offset;
441
442        for n in 0..4.min(remaining) {
443            code = (code << 8) | bytes[offset + n] as u32;
444
445            if self.encoding.lookup_cid_code(code, (n + 1) as u8).is_some() {
446                return (code, n + 1);
447            }
448        }
449
450        (0, 1)
451    }
452
453    pub(crate) fn origin_displacement(&self, code: u32) -> Vec2 {
454        let cid = self.code_to_cid(code).unwrap_or(0);
455
456        if self.is_horizontal() {
457            Vec2::default()
458        } else if let Some([_, v1, v2]) = self.widths2.get(&cid) {
459            Vec2::new(-*v1 as f64, -*v2 as f64)
460        } else {
461            Vec2::new(-self.horizontal_width(cid) as f64 / 2.0, -self.dw2.0 as f64)
462        }
463    }

465    /// The text a character code stands for, or `None` when the font gives none (or, for an
466    /// identity `/ToUnicode` name, when the code is a control or a lone surrogate).
467    pub(crate) fn char_code_to_unicode(&self, code: u32) -> Option<BfString> {
468        if self.identity_to_unicode {
469            // Controls and lone surrogates are not text. The same rule builds the editing
470            // map, `identity_to_unicode` in crates/fonts/src/pdf.rs: keep both alike.
471            return char::from_u32(code).filter(|c| !c.is_control()).map(BfString::Char);
472        }
473        if let Some(to_unicode) = &self.to_unicode {
474            let key = if self.to_unicode_is_cid_indexed { self.code_to_cid(code).unwrap_or(0) } else { code };
475            // PdfCraft patch (85): a `/ToUnicode` written as a CID CMap (`begincidrange` /
476            // `begincidchar`, whose destinations are numbers) gives the code's Unicode value as
477            // that number, as glyph lookup already reads it (`map_via_unicode`) and as pdftotext
478            // and PDFium extract it. ISO 32000-2 §9.10.3 has `beginbfrange` / `beginbfchar` here;
479            // Word writes CID ranges, and such text extracted nothing.
480            if let Some(s) = to_unicode.lookup_bf_string(key).or_else(|| {
481                (1..=4).find_map(|len| to_unicode.lookup_cid_code(key, len).and_then(|cid| char::from_u32(cid.to_u32()))).map(BfString::Char)
482            }) {
483                return Some(s);
484            }
485        }
486        // PdfCraft patch (84): then the collection's UCS2 CMap, by the code's CID.
487        if let Some(ucs2) = self.ucs2.as_ref().and_then(Ucs2::cmap)
488            && let Some(s) = self.code_to_cid(code).and_then(|cid| ucs2.lookup_bf_string(cid))
489        {
490            return Some(s);
491        }
492
493        None
494    }
495}

497/// PdfCraft patch (84): a collection's UCS2 CMap, parsed the first time a code needs it: a font
498/// whose `/ToUnicode` maps every code it shows never parses it.
499struct Ucs2 {
500    data: &'static [u8],
501    resolver: CMapResolverFn,
502    map: OnceLock<Option<CMap>>,
503}
504
505impl Ucs2 {
506    fn parse(&self) -> Option<CMap> {
507        let resolver = self.resolver.clone();
508        CMap::parse(self.data, move |n| (resolver)(n))
509    }
510
511    fn cmap(&self) -> Option<&CMap> {
512        self.map.get_or_init(|| self.parse()).as_ref()
513    }
514}
515
516impl std::fmt::Debug for Ucs2 {
517    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
518        f.debug_struct("Ucs2").field("bytes", &self.data.len()).finish_non_exhaustive()
519    }
520}

528#[derive(Debug)]
529enum FontType {
530    /// An OpenType font.
531    OpenType(OpenTypeFontBlob),
532    /// A CFF font.
533    Cff(CffFontBlob),
534    /// A Type1 font. (Yes, there actually exist PDFs that embed a Type1 font in a
535    /// CID font :))
536    Type1(Type1FontBlob),
537}
538
539impl FontType {
540    fn new(descriptor: &Dict<'_>) -> Option<Self> {
541        // PDF has a distinction between CIDFontType0 and CIDFontType 2, with
542        // specific requirements what font type can appear where. However, some
543        // PDFs use wrong metadata, so we simply bruteforce without even looking
544        // at the metadata.
545
546        let data = descriptor
547            .get::<Stream<'_>>(FONT_FILE2)
548            .or_else(|| descriptor.get::<Stream<'_>>(FONT_FILE3))
549            // See PDFBOX-2599. Apparently, Acrobat accepts this as well.
550            .or_else(|| descriptor.get::<Stream<'_>>(FONT_FILE))?
551            .decoded()
552            .ok()?;
553
554        let data = Arc::new(data.into_owned());
555
556        let parsed = if let Ok(_font_ref) = FontRef::from_index(data.as_ref(), 0) {
557            // It's an OpenType font, either TrueType or CFF.
558            Self::OpenType(OpenTypeFontBlob::new(data, 0)?)
559        } else if let Some(cff) = CffFontBlob::new(data.clone()) {
560            // It's a CFF font.
561            Self::Cff(cff)
562        } else if let Some(t1) = Type1FontBlob::new(data) {
563            // It's a Type1 (PFB) font.
564            Self::Type1(t1)
565        } else {
566            return None;
567        };
568
569        Some(parsed)
570    }
571}

573#[derive(Debug, Default)]
574enum CidToGIdMap {
575    #[default]
576    Identity,
577    Mapped {
578        forward: HashMap<u16, GlyphId>,
579        inverse: HashMap<GlyphId, u16>,
580    },
581}
582
583impl CidToGIdMap {
584    fn new(dict: &Dict<'_>) -> Option<Self> {
585        if let Some(name) = dict.get::<Name<'_>>(CID_TO_GID_MAP) {
586            if name.deref() == IDENTITY { Some(Self::Identity) } else { None }
587        } else if let Some(stream) = dict.get::<Stream<'_>>(CID_TO_GID_MAP) {
588            let decoded = stream.decoded().ok()?;
589            let mut forward = HashMap::new();
590            let mut inverse = HashMap::new();
591
592            for (cid, gid) in decoded.chunks_exact(2).enumerate() {
593                let gid = GlyphId::new(u16::from_be_bytes([gid[0], gid[1]]) as u32);
594
595                forward.insert(cid as u16, gid);
596                inverse.insert(gid, cid as u16);
597            }
598
599            Some(Self::Mapped { forward, inverse })
600        } else {
601            None
602        }
603    }
604
605    fn map(&self, code: u16) -> GlyphId {
606        match self {
607            Self::Identity => GlyphId::new(code as u32),
608            Self::Mapped { forward, .. } => forward.get(&code).copied().unwrap_or(GlyphId::NOTDEF),
609        }
610    }
611
612    fn inverse_map(&self, gid: GlyphId) -> u16 {
613        match self {
614            Self::Identity => gid.to_u32() as u16,
615            Self::Mapped { inverse, .. } => inverse.get(&gid).copied().unwrap_or(gid.to_u32() as u16),
616        }
617    }
618}

620/// PdfCraft patch: Variation Selectors (U+FE00–U+FE0F) and their supplement (U+E0100–U+E01EF).
621fn is_variation_selector(c: char) -> bool {
622    matches!(c, '\u{FE00}'..='\u{FE0F}' | '\u{E0100}'..='\u{E01EF}')
623}
624
625/// PdfCraft patch: whether `name`, a `/BaseFont` without its subset tag, is one of the four
626/// faces of Arial or Times New Roman as exporters name them: `ArialMT`, `Arial-BoldMT`,
627/// `Arial-ItalicMT`, `Arial-BoldItalicMT`, `TimesNewRomanPSMT`, `TimesNewRomanPS-BoldMT` and so
628/// on, or `Arial` or `TimesNewRoman` followed by `,Bold`, `,Italic` or `,BoldItalic`. Both
629/// number their first 258 glyphs in the standard Macintosh order. Arial Narrow, Arial Black,
630/// Arial Unicode MS and Arial Rounded are other fonts, numbered their own way. Letter case
631/// doesn't matter, `MT` included.
632fn numbers_glyphs_in_mac_order(name: &str) -> bool {
633    let (family, style) = name.split_once([',', '-', ' ']).unwrap_or((name, ""));
634    let style: String = style.chars().filter(|c| !matches!(c, ',' | '-' | ' ')).collect();
635    ["Arial", "TimesNewRoman", "TimesNewRomanPS"].iter().any(|f| without_mt(family).eq_ignore_ascii_case(f))
636        && ["", "Regular", "Bold", "Italic", "BoldItalic"].iter().any(|s| without_mt(&style).eq_ignore_ascii_case(s))
637}
638
639/// PdfCraft patch: `name` without a trailing `MT` in any letter case (Monotype's mark in
640/// PostScript names such as `ArialMT`).
641fn without_mt(name: &str) -> &str {
642    name.len()
643        .checked_sub(2)
644        .and_then(|stem| Some((name.get(..stem)?, name.get(stem..)?)))
645        .filter(|(_, suffix)| suffix.eq_ignore_ascii_case("MT"))
646        .map_or(name, |(stem, _)| stem)
647}

649/// PdfCraft patch: the largest CID (ISO 32000-2 §9.7.2; CIDs are at most two bytes).
650const MAX_CID: u32 = 65_535;
651
652fn read_widths(arr: &Array<'_>) -> Option<HashMap<u32, f32>> {
653    let mut map = HashMap::new();
654    let mut iter = arr.flex_iter();
655
656    loop {
657        if let Some((mut first, range)) = iter.next::<(u32, Array<'_>)>() {
658            for width in range.iter::<f32>() {
659                if first > MAX_CID {
660                    break;
661                }
662                map.insert(first, width);
663                first = first.checked_add(1)?;
664            }
665        } else if let Some((first, second, width)) = iter.next::<(u32, u32, f32)>() {
666            // PdfCraft patch: CIDs stop at 65535. A corrupt range such as
667            // `0 4294967295 500` inserted billions of entries (found by fuzzing).
668            for i in first..=second.min(MAX_CID) {
669                map.insert(i, width);
670            }
671        } else {
672            break;
673        }
674    }
675
676    Some(map)
677}
678
679fn read_widths2(arr: &Array<'_>) -> Option<HashMap<u32, [f32; 3]>> {
680    let mut map = HashMap::new();
681    let mut iter = arr.flex_iter();
682
683    loop {
684        if let Some((mut first, range)) = iter.next::<(u32, Array<'_>)>() {
685            let mut iter = range.iter::<f32>();
686
687            while let Some(w) = iter.next() {
688                // PdfCraft patch: as in `read_widths`, checked before the run's metrics are
689                // read. Without it, a run starting at 4294967295 overflowed `first` and
690                // discarded the whole /W2 table.
691                if first > MAX_CID {
692                    break;
693                }
694                let v1 = iter.next()?;
695                let v2 = iter.next()?;
696                map.insert(first, [w, v1, v2]);
697                first = first.checked_add(1)?;
698            }
699        } else if let Some((first, second, w, v1, v2)) = iter.next::<(u32, u32, f32, f32, f32)>() {
700            // PdfCraft patch: as in `read_widths`.
701            for i in first..=second.min(MAX_CID) {
702                map.insert(i, [w, v1, v2]);
703            }
704        } else {
705            break;
706        }
707    }
708
709    Some(map)
710}
711
712fn read_cid_system_info(descendant_font: &Dict<'_>) -> Option<CharacterCollection> {
713    let info = descendant_font.get::<Dict<'_>>(CIDSYSTEMINFO)?;
714    let registry = info.get::<object::String<'_>>(REGISTRY)?;
715    let ordering = info.get::<object::String<'_>>(ORDERING)?;
716    let supplement = info.get::<i32>(SUPPLEMENT).unwrap_or(0);
717    let family = CidFamily::from_registry_ordering(registry.deref(), ordering.deref());
718
719    Some(CharacterCollection { family, supplement })
720}
721
722fn read_encoding(object: &Object<'_>, cmap_resolver: &CMapResolverFn) -> Option<CMap> {
723    // TODO: Support fetching CMaps referenced via `usecmap` in the PDF.
724    match object {
725        Object::Name(n) => {
726            let cmap_type = crate::third_party::hayro_cmap::CMapName::from_bytes(n.deref());
727            match cmap_type {
728                crate::third_party::hayro_cmap::CMapName::IdentityH => Some(CMap::identity_h()),
729                crate::third_party::hayro_cmap::CMapName::IdentityV => Some(CMap::identity_v()),
730                _ => {
731                    let data = (cmap_resolver)(cmap_type)?;
732                    let resolver = cmap_resolver.clone();
733                    CMap::parse(data, move |n| (resolver)(n))
734                }
735            }
736        }
737        Object::Stream(s) => {
738            let decoded = s.decoded().ok()?;
739            let resolver = cmap_resolver.clone();
740            CMap::parse(&decoded, move |n| (resolver)(n))
741        }
742        _ => None,
743    }
744}

746/// PdfCraft patch test (ported from craft-libs): a /W2 run whose first CID is past `MAX_CID`
747/// is skipped and the rest of the table kept.
748#[cfg(any())]
749mod tests {
750    use super::read_widths2;
751    use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::object::{Array, FromBytes};
752
753    #[cfg(any())]
754    fn w2_run_past_the_largest_cid_keeps_the_rest_of_the_table() {
755        let arr = Array::from_bytes(b"[4294967295 [1000 500] 10 [900 450 860] 20 30 800 400 870]").unwrap();
756        let map = read_widths2(&arr).unwrap();
757
758        assert_eq!(map.get(&4_294_967_295), None);
759        assert_eq!(map.get(&10), Some(&[900.0, 450.0, 860.0]));
760        assert_eq!(map.get(&25), Some(&[800.0, 400.0, 870.0]));
761        assert_eq!(map.len(), 12);
762    }
763}

765#[cfg(any())]
766mod width_tests {
767    use super::*;
768    use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::Pdf;
769    use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::object::ObjectIdentifier;
770
771    /// A PDF whose object 5 is `array`, for what references in it can reach.
772    fn with_array(array: &str) -> Pdf {
773        let pdf = format!(
774            "%PDF-1.7\n1 0 obj << /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >> endobj\n\
775             2 0 obj << /Type /Pages /Kids [3 0 R] /Count 1 >> endobj\n\
776             3 0 obj << /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 10 10] >> endobj\n\
777             4 0 obj 20 endobj\n5 0 obj {array} endobj\n6 0 obj 22 endobj\n\
778             7 0 obj 7 0 R endobj\n8 0 obj 9 0 R endobj\n9 0 obj 8 0 R endobj\n\
779             10 0 obj 4 0 R endobj\n11 0 obj [500 600] endobj\n12 0 obj [-1000 500 880] endobj\n\
780             trailer << /Root 1 0 R >>\n%%EOF\n"
781        );
782        Pdf::new(pdf.into_bytes()).unwrap()
783    }
784
785    /// `/W` and `/W2` read groups of items, and either kind can start with a reference: taken for
786    /// the whole group it was lost, with all that followed, and those glyphs fell back to `/DW`.
787    #[cfg(any())]
788    fn a_width_group_can_start_with_a_reference() {
789        let widths = |array: &str| {
790            let pdf = with_array(array);
791            let array = pdf.xref().get::<Array<'_>>(ObjectIdentifier::new(5, 0)).unwrap();
792            let mut read: Vec<_> = read_widths(&array).unwrap().into_iter().collect();
793            read.sort_by_key(|(cid, _)| *cid);
794            read
795        };
796        let by_list = vec![(20, 500.0), (21, 600.0)];
797        assert_eq!(widths("[20 [500 600]]"), by_list);
798        assert_eq!(widths("[4 0 R [500 600]]"), by_list);
799        let by_range = vec![(20, 700.0), (21, 700.0), (22, 700.0)];
800        assert_eq!(widths("[20 22 700]"), by_range);
801        assert_eq!(widths("[4 0 R 22 700]"), by_range);
802        assert_eq!(widths("[4 0 R 6 0 R 700]"), by_range);
803        assert_eq!(widths("[1 [100] 4 0 R [500 600]]"), vec![(1, 100.0), (20, 500.0), (21, 600.0)], "after a group");
804
805        let vertical = |array: &str| {
806            let pdf = with_array(array);
807            let array = pdf.xref().get::<Array<'_>>(ObjectIdentifier::new(5, 0)).unwrap();
808            let mut read: Vec<_> = read_widths2(&array).unwrap().into_iter().collect();
809            read.sort_by_key(|(cid, _)| *cid);
810            read
811        };
812        let by_list = vec![(20, [-1000.0, 500.0, 880.0])];
813        assert_eq!(vertical("[20 [-1000 500 880]]"), by_list);
814        assert_eq!(vertical("[4 0 R [-1000 500 880]]"), by_list);
815        let by_range = vec![(20, [-900.0, 400.0, 800.0]), (21, [-900.0, 400.0, 800.0]), (22, [-900.0, 400.0, 800.0])];
816        assert_eq!(vertical("[20 22 -900 400 800]"), by_range);
817        assert_eq!(vertical("[4 0 R 22 -900 400 800]"), by_range);
818
819        // A group's list can be given by reference too, and a reference to a reference is what it
820        // names.
821        let by_list = vec![(20, 500.0), (21, 600.0)];
822        assert_eq!(widths("[20 11 0 R]"), by_list);
823        assert_eq!(widths("[10 0 R [500 600]]"), by_list);
824        assert_eq!(widths("[10 0 R 11 0 R]"), by_list);
825        assert_eq!(vertical("[20 12 0 R]"), vec![(20, [-1000.0, 500.0, 880.0])]);
826
827        // A reference that only leads back to itself holds no number, so those glyphs keep `/DW`.
828        for array in ["[7 0 R [500 600]]", "[8 0 R [500 600]]", "[20 7 0 R 700]", "[7 0 R 8 0 R 700]", "[20 [7 0 R 600]]"] {
829            assert!(widths(array).is_empty(), "{array}");
830        }
831        for array in ["[7 0 R [-1000 500 880]]", "[8 0 R 22 -900 400 800]", "[20 [7 0 R 500 880]]"] {
832            assert!(vertical(array).is_empty(), "{array}");
833        }
834    }
835}
